question: The analysis of the data obtained from cases of Ebola virus disease in Guinea and Sierra Leone, allows us to affirm that:

options.opa: The mortality of the infection exceeds 85%.
options.opb: The treatment is based on support measures (hydroelectrolitic replenishment i.v. and antibiotics).
options.opc: More than half of the cases correspond to health personnel.
options.opd: Gastrointestinal hemorrhage is a common cause of mortality.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ebola virus disease" -> "high mortality rate" -> "mortality exceeds -> 85%
CHAIN: "Ebola virus disease" -> "supportive treatment" -> "hydroelectrolytic replenishment i.v." -> "antibiotics" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Ebola virus disease" -> "health personnel exposure" -> "more than half of cases" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Ebola virus disease" -> "gastrointestinal symptoms" -> "gastrointestinal hemorrhage" -> "common cause of mortality" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Ebola virus disease" -> "age-related mortality" -> "higher in adolescents" -> 40%
enhanced_information: The mortality rate of Ebola virus disease does not exceed 85%; it is typically around 50-70%. The treatment for Ebola is primarily supportive, focusing on intravenous fluid replenishment and managing symptoms, but antibiotics are not a standard treatment unless there is a secondary bacterial infection. Health personnel are at high risk, but they do not constitute more than half of the cases. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage can occur in Ebola, but it is not the most common cause of mortality; multi-organ failure and shock are more typical. Mortality is generally higher in young children and older adults, not specifically in adolescents. The retrieved evidence paths about gastrointestinal symptoms and hemorrhage are too broad and not directly relevant to Ebola's specific mortality causes.
analysis: The mortality rate of Ebola virus disease is typically around 50-70%, not exceeding 85%, which rules out option opa. The treatment for Ebola is primarily supportive, focusing on intravenous fluid replenishment and managing symptoms, which aligns with option opb, although antibiotics are not standard unless there is a secondary bacterial infection. Health personnel are at high risk but do not make up more than half of the cases, eliminating option opc. Gastrointestinal hemorrhage can occur but is not the most common cause of mortality; multi-organ failure and shock are more typical, which makes option opd less likely. Mortality is generally higher in young children and older adults, not specifically in adolescents, ruling out option ope. Therefore, the most accurate statement based on standard medical knowledge is that the treatment is based on support measures, making option opb the best choice.
